song.title: You Shook Me All Night Long

guitar.notes: Iconic, extremely well-documented pairing: Angus's Gibson SG and Malcolm's Gretsch (Jet Firebird/Gretsch 6131) rhythm guitar are core to AC/DC's image.

tone.target: bright crunchy AC/DC rhythm with tight upper mids
tone.profile: bright crunchy AC/DC rhythm with tight upper mids
tone.summary: A classic British rhythm setup using the UK 45 amp model for raw JTM/Plexi crunch, paired with a UK Vintage 4x12 cab. The signal chain emphasizes tight compression, an OD boost for bite, and minimal modulation to achieve AC/DC's signature punchy sound.
corrections: keep gain lower than modern mid-gain
favor raw Plexi/JTM crunch over JCM heaviness

rig.name: AC/DC - You Shook Me All Night Long - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and pick noise inherent in high-gain rhythm playing.
Provide a tight, punchy boost and slight grit to enhance the pick attack and upper mids (JTM/Plexi style).

alternatives.reason: Good alternative for general crunch, but Green OD is better suited for the specific bite required.

blocks.purpose: Add foundational crunch and grit without excessive fuzz or modern scooped gain. Acts as a secondary drive stage.
blocks.gap: The RAT is versatile, but careful settings are needed to avoid sounding too aggressive; it helps achieve the raw 'crunch' feel.

alternatives.reason: Too general; RAT-style offers a more vintage, biting edge.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the raw, punchy British tone (JTM/Plexi) required for AC/DC's rhythm sound.

alternatives.reason: Slightly more modern; UK 45 captures the raw, early-to-mid 70s bite better.

proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and aggression in the mids.
